input.reasoning_summary: All three challenges have been refuted by the evidence. H1 challenged whether consolidated gross margin might have increased or remained stable, but E9 from the fiscal 2026 10-K explicitly shows that consolidated gross margin decreased 100 basis points. H2 challenged whether tariff impacts were fully offset, but E15 explicitly quantifies that tariffs contributed 50 basis points to the gross margin decline in Q3 FY2026, and E10 and E11 show tariffs drove margin declines that were only partially offset by productivity and pricing. H3 challenged whether the evidence was only segment-level, but E9 provides consolidated company-level data showing the gross margin decline, and E15 explicitly attributes part of the quarterly decline to tariffs at the consolidated level. The newly retrieved evidence strengthens the initial verdict: E9 confirms the consolidated gross margin declined in fiscal 2026, and E15 explicitly quantifies the tariff impact at 50 basis points for Q3. Combined with the original evidence (E1-E6, E10-E11) showing consistent tariff impacts across multiple segments and quarters throughout fiscal 2026, the claim that tariffs had "no effect" on P&G's gross margin in fiscal 2026 is clearly contradicted.
